action.rationale: Fresh 20D problem with a total budget of 100 and noisy evaluations; per policy, spending ~12% (~12 evals) on probes is affordable and helps reveal modality and scale. Probe results go into the archive, improving warm starts and de-risking method choice before we commit.

20D, cheap but noisy objective with a huge value spread (log10_range=6.26) and weak global structure (fdc_spearman=0.1748) suggests multiple basins. With 88 evals left, a small race between TuRBO and CMA-ES—both robust in noisy, high-D landscapes—will identify the better driver before committing more budget. Probes already used 12/100, incumbent y=388655.62.

CMA-ES won the race decisively (230,733 vs 634,033 over 12 evals each), is not converged (sigma 2.77, popsize 12), and has not yet run post-race (evals_in_tenure 0). With 64 evals left, giving it ~5 generations to exploit its momentum is prudent on this noisy 20D problem.
